big: An investor holds shares and fears a sharp fall. A protective put works like insurance: it limits losses below the strike, for the price of the premium. Strategies can protect. Speculation is a different matter.

lines: None is without risk. A protective put limits a fall but costs a premium. A covered call earns premium but caps your gain. A straddle bets on a big move in either direction. A bull call spread cuts cost and caps both profit and loss. This is education, not a call to trade.

title: Simple strategies
stops: A protective put limits losses below the strike
A covered call has no cap on the gain
A straddle profits from a big move either way
A bull call spread has unlimited profit
caps: It caps both profit and loss.

q: An investor holds shares and buys a put to guard against a sharp fall. What is this?
why: A covered call sells a call.
A put on shares you own limits losses.
A straddle buys a call and a put.
A bull call spread uses two calls.

why: The seller collects premium but agrees to sell at the strike.

q: A trader expects a big move after results but is unsure of the direction. Which strategy matches?
why: A covered call suits a quiet market.
A protective put protects held shares.
A straddle profits from a big move either way.
A bull call spread bets on a rise.

q: A trader buys a ₹500 call and sells a ₹550 call. What is the effect?
opts: Unlimited profit on a rise in price
Unlimited loss on a fall in price
No premium at all, paid or received
Cheaper, with profit and loss capped
why: The profit is capped. It does not fit the facts given.
The loss is capped at the net premium. The details here point elsewhere.
Premiums are still paid and received. The details here point elsewhere.
Selling the higher call cuts cost but caps profit.

pts: Protective put: insurance for shares, costs a premium.
Covered call: earns premium, caps gain. Straddle: bets on a big move.
Bull call spread: cheaper, with capped profit and loss.
